paper_metadata.title: Intracerebral Hemorrhage in COVID-19 Patients with Pulmonary Failure: A Propensity Score-Matched Registry Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study clearly defines the source population (tertiary center), recruitment period, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. While it is a single-center retrospective study, the use of ICD-10 codes and consecutive enrollment of COVID-19 patients minimizes selection bias within that setting.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: University Hospital of Freiburg, Germany... a tertiary treatment center for ARDS and ECMO-therapy
items.reasoning: The setting and nature of the center are explicitly stated.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Patients with non-COVID-19 ARDS (ICD-10 code J80.01; J80.02; J80.03; J80.03; J80.09) were extracted from the hospital data system
items.reasoning: The use of specific ICD-10 codes for the control group and PCR confirmation for the COVID group is a robust identification method.

items.evidence_snippet: from 01/01/2018 to 05/31/2020 (non-COVID-19 group). Critically ill patients with PCR-confrmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and ARDS were enrolled from 03/2020 to 05/2020
items.reasoning: Specific dates are provided for both cohorts.

items.evidence_snippet: We excluded patients younger than 18 years and with an intensive care unit (ICU) stay of less than 24 h. Also, patients with mild ARDS according to the Berlin defnition were excluded.
items.reasoning: Clear age, duration of stay, and disease severity criteria are listed.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (ICH) was measured using objective imaging (CT/MRI). However, imaging was only performed in 58.3% of patients based on clinical suspicion, which introduces a risk of missing asymptomatic or 'clinically silent' ICH cases, potentially underestimating the incidence.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: ICH was detected using cerebral computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined by imaging findings.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: An experienced radiologist and neurologist reviewed the scans in detail
items.reasoning: While expert review was used, there is no mention of blinding the radiologist to the COVID-19 status.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Cerebral imaging was done in patients suspected of a cerebral pathology or in cases of prolonged awakening.
items.reasoning: The criteria for imaging were consistent, but not all patients were imaged (58.3%), which is a limitation noted by the authors.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used Propensity Score Matching (PSM) to account for key confounders including age, VV-ECMO, and bleeding risk (HAS-BLED). This is a robust method for addressing observed confounding in observational data.

items.reasoning: Key clinical confounders for ICH in this population were identified and measured.
